The task is monumentally difficult; she needs to synthesize noise that is both random and structurally meaningless enough not to be classified as an attack vector by the Entity’s integrated intelligence. "We are looking for a signature of informational entropy," she explains, her voice dropping to a highly focused murmur. "It must contain high-frequency jitter and unpredictable phase shifts across multiple carrier bands—the statistical equivalent of white noise generated by pure dimensional distortion."

She pulls up a complex graph, showing overlapping wave forms that represent the difference between "noise" and "coherent signal." "A standard random generator will fail," she warns, tracing a sharp peak on the screen. "The Entity’s pattern recognition is too advanced for simple randomness; it anticipates chaos. THE IMPERFECT SOLUTION

Ren presents a synthesized waveform. "I can generate a prototype signature, but it will be based on historical Veil probes—highly corrupted data remnants," she reports. "It won't be pure, and it carries the risk of carrying latent, unpredictable signal degradation."

"If we use corrupted probe data," she states flatly, "we are introducing a known variable into an unknown system. It risks destabilizing the injection entirely before it can even reach the target."

THE JUNCTURE

The solution is mathematically sound but practically fraught with risk. Ren needs the final operational command to begin synthesizing and tuning the prototype signature, which requires a significant amount of time on her console. She looks at you, waiting for the decision that balances scientific necessity against immediate systemic peril.

She waits for your assessment of this new level of complexity.
